opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Mann (employee ID E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E027.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Mann (E027) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is within the allowed level for a full-time Engineer owning the system. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E027 (Jacob Mann) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors get read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write exceeds the max allowed (read), so recommend granting read for Source Code.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR's note says E027 is full-time (recommend write), while the Security record says E027 is a contractor with basic security training, whose maximum is read (write requires advanced training). Because the records disagree and granting write would violate policy if the security record is correct, I grant the more restrictive allowed level, read — which is at or below the maximum under either the contractor interpretation and never exceeds the requested level.
